task_instance: Wrote a small C program (vuln.c) containing an intentional 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow (malloc(10) then write to buf[10]), compiled it with `clang -fsanitize=address -g -o vuln_asan vuln.c` per the skill's Step 1, ran it with `ASAN_OPTIONS=verbosity=1:abort_on_error=1 ./vuln_asan` per Steps 2-3, and confirmed ASan detected and reported the heap-buffer-overflow with a full stack trace and shadow memory map, then aborted the process (exit 134). Also verified combining sanitizers works via `clang -fsanitize=address,undefined -g -o vuln_asan_ubsan vuln.c`.
evidence: cd into work dir; `clang --version` -> Ubuntu clang 18.1.3; wrote vuln.c with `buf[10] = 'X'` overflow after `malloc(10)`; `clang -fsanitize=address -g -o vuln_asan vuln.c` exited 0; `ASAN_OPTIONS=verbosity=1:abort_on_error=1 ./vuln_asan` printed verbosity=1 startup diagnostics (shadow memory layout, redzone size, interceptor init) confirming ASan was active, then produced: '==PID==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow on address 0x50200000001a ... WRITE of size 1 at 0x50200000001a thread T0 #0 ... in main vuln.c:9:13' with allocation traceback pointing to vuln.c:6:25 (the malloc site), a shadow-byte map, and 'SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow vuln.c:9:13 in main', ending in '==PID==ABORTING' (process exit code 134, i.e. SIGABRT, matching abort_on_error=1). This matches the skill's Quick Reference/Step 1-3 workflow and the example ASan report format shown in the skill doc. Additionally compiled with `-fsanitize=address,undefined` successfully (exit 0) to confirm the 'Combining Sanitizers' pattern also works. Files produced: /tmp/.../vuln.c, vuln_asan, vuln_asan_ubsan (all inside the work directory).
